devin: FYI nightly benchmark shows a regression in paged-attn runs — p99 up ~12% and throughput down ~8% on the kv-pager job. started around the slotmap change.

maya: repro steps? can you paste the perf command and a short trace?

devin: repro is straightforward: `./bench --model paged-attn --kernel auto --batch 16 --seq 1024 --iters 500`
logs:```
[2026-03-17 02:12:11] kernel-chooser: picked flashv2 for batch=16,seq=1024
[2026-03-17 02:12:11] kv-pager: reclaim-trigger: eviction windows=3, reclaiming 8 slots
[2026-03-17 02:12:11] runtime: blocking on slot-reclaim (50ms)
[2026-03-17 02:12:11] kernel-chooser: fallback to flashv1 due to timeout
```
This pattern repeats and lines up with the latency spikes.

eric: interesting — sounds like a race between the kernel selection path and the background pager reclaim. if the chooser waits for a KV slot it times out and picks a slower kernel. that flip costs ~30-60us per token on our microbench.

sasha: can you dump the slotmap stats (counts/free list lengths) before/after the reclaim? i want to see if the reclaim is fragmenting the slab and leaving tiny islands that the fast allocator can't satisfy.

devin: pasted short snapshot:```
slotmap_total=4096
free_list_len=6
fragment_runs=122
largest_free_run=4
avg_run=1.2
reclaim_cycles=3
```
looks like frequent small frees -> heavy fragmentation. reclaim seems aggressive and runs during hot requests.

maya: that matches the profiler: stack traces show kernel-chooser waiting at `wait_for_slot_or_timeout()` in the hot path. attaching flame snippet: `chooser -> wait_for_slot_or_timeout -> pager_reclaim` (hot).

eric: two quick hypotheses: 1) reclaim runs synchronously on allocation path when under pressure (bad) 2) the kernel chooser has a too-short timeout and prefers kernel flip rather than backing off to batching strategy. both would cause oscillation.

sasha: simple mitigation patch idea: introduce a short local reclaim window and opportunistic batching preference. pseudocode:```c
if (pager_pressure && free_list_len < LOCAL_THRESHOLD) {
  if (batch_size >= PREF_BATCH) {
    prefer_small_kernel = false; // keep fast kernel
    schedule_background_reclaim();
    spin_short(8us); // wait for local free to appear
  } else {
    prefer_small_kernel = true; // avoid flip cost
  }
}
```
this keeps chooser from flipping to slower kernel during transient pressure.

devin: tried a quick branch with spin_short(8us) + schedule_background_reclaim(); on microbench p99 dropped back ~9% and throughput recovered most of the delta. need more runs for stability.

maya: can you push the branch to a test pipeline and run the nightly kv-pager job? also add telemetry: increment a `chooser_reclaimed_waits` counter so we can correlate.

ci-bot: nightly-job:240111_kvpager_regress (job id 8723) queued. artifacts: https://ci.internal/8723/logs

eric: long-term we should separate reclaim scheduling from allocation hot-path entirely — use a per-shard async recycler with capacity smoothing. also adjust kernel-chooser to consider `reclaim_inflight` flag before deciding.

sasha: agreed. i'll open a small RFC for async recycler + chooser tweak. will include perf goals and a few microbench patches.

devin: for now i'll stabilize the spin/wait patch, add telemetry, and run more scenarios (vary batch sizes 1/4/16/32, seq 256/512/1024) and post results. thanks. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks team. if nightly flakiness persists raise a canary for dedicated nodes so customers don't see regressions.

devin: noted — will do.
